answer: Each identity claims a jetty bollard, locks a 70-credit bond, and torques ferrous bolts with a quartz gauge, filing torque, serial. An auditor recomputes expected torque from the jetty torque-angle table and checks each quartz serial appears once. Torque off by over 3 percent, a reused serial, or one bolt for two identities burns the bond. First filing costs 38; the k-th costs 38+6(k-1), so the 1,000th costs 6,032 and 1,000 fakes pay 3,035,000 plus 70,000 at risk. A rented-torque ring fails, since a rented serial is already on the board. An honest operator pays 38 once and recovers its bond.
